title: pricing-packaging-back-of-envelope-notes-v11
content:
Back-of-envelope pricing + unit-economics notes (personal scratchpad)

Context / goal:
- Quick gut-checks for hosted API pricing tiers, dedicated commitments, and embedding pricing.
- Keep the math simple and flag assumptions. Use for internal spike + deck later.

Key assumptions (placeholder, update with infra numbers from infra-costs spreadsheet):
- GPU hourly cost (effective cost to Redwood after infra, amortization, and ops): $3.00/hour (spot/pooled avg) => baseline.
- Inference throughput (tokens generated per second) varies by model/precision. Example buckets:
  * Small-ish quantized model (7B q4): 200 tokens/sec
  * Medium model (13B q4): 120 tokens/sec
  * Large model (70B optimized): 30 tokens/sec
- Batching & caching can reduce effective cost per token by ~1.5x-4x depending on workload (we'll param later).
- Network, storage, and control-plane costs: add ~15-25% overhead to raw GPU cost (accounted separately).
- Desired gross margin target for hosted API: 40-60% (depends on growth vs. profitability).

Basic token math (single GPU, no caching, no batching):
- tokens/hr = tokens/sec * 3600
- cost/token = GPU $/hr / tokens/hr

Example 1 — 7B model (200 tps):
- tokens/hr = 200 * 3600 = 720,000 tokens/hr
- cost/token = $3 / 720,000 = $0.00000417 (~$4.17 per 1M tokens)
- add infra+ops overhead (20%) => $0.0000050/token (~$5.00 per 1M tokens)
- add margin target 50% => list price ~ $0.00001/token (~$10 per 1M tokens)

Example 2 — 13B model (120 tps):
- tokens/hr = 120 * 3600 = 432,000 tokens/hr
- cost/token = $3 / 432,000 = $0.00000694 (~$6.94 per 1M tokens)
- +20% overhead => ~$8.33 per 1M tokens => list price @50% margin => ~$16.7 per 1M tokens

Example 3 — 70B model (30 tps):
- tokens/hr = 30 * 3600 = 108,000 tokens/hr
- cost/token = $3 / 108,000 = $0.00002778 (~$27.8 per 1M tokens)
- +20% overhead => ~$33.3 per 1M tokens => list price @50% margin => ~$66.6 per 1M tokens

Notes:
- These numbers are intentionally back-of-envelope. Actual per-token cost heavily depends on: kernel efficiency, sequence length distribution, KV cache hits (for chat-like workflows), batching, and fractional GPU utilization (idle time).
- Caching effect: prefix caching (customer-level) and response caching can cut downstream token generation by 20-70% depending on workload. For prompt-heavy use (many repeated system prompts), effective cost goes way down.
- Batching: synchronous low-latency workloads have limited batching (~1.0-1.3x). Async embeddings and batch generation can get 2-4x efficiency.

Embedding math (rough):
- Embedding throughput tends to be higher (smaller model, optimized ops). Example: 2000 embeddings/sec on medium instance => 7.2M embeddings/hr.
- If GPU $3/hr => cost/embedding = $3 / 7,200,000 = $0.00000042 (~$0.42 per 1M embeddings)
- Add overhead (20%) => ~$0.50 per 1M embeddings. List price @50% margin => ~$1.00 per 1M embeddings
- Empirical sanity check: market embedding prices range ~$0.20-$3.00 per 1M (depending on vector dim & model). Our number is plausible for a fast, optimized open-model embedder.

Suggested hosted pay-as-you-go pricing (starter ideas):
- Free tier: 100k tokens/month + 5k embeddings (token-only throttle).
- Pay-as-you-go (no commitment): $10 per 1M tokens (default generation endpoint, mixed model pool) — reflects blended mix of models and ops overhead.
- Embeddings PAYG: $1.00 per 1M embeddings (rounded).
- Notes on PAYG: keep simple for dev adoption, losses on tiny usage ok to encourage growth.

Commit / reserved pricing (Dedicated-like offers):
- For teams that commit monthly usage we give deep discounts. Two levers: committed tokens/month or reserved GPUs/month.
- Example token-commit tiers:
  * Commit 100M tokens/mo => 35% discount off PAYG => $6.50 per 1M effective
  * Commit 500M tokens/mo => 55% discount => $4.50 per 1M
  * Commit 2B tokens/mo => 70% discount => $3.00 per 1M (requires dedicated capacity)
- Alternatively, reserved nodes: price per GPU/month (dedicated infra) + small per-token ops fee. Example: reserved 1x A100 equiv = $2000/mo (internal pricing to compute), include baseline throughput, then burst PAYG. (Need infra numbers to refine.)

Suggested SKU examples (for packaging/website):
- Starter (free): 100k tokens / mo, 5k embeddings, basic rate limits, community support.
- Developer (self-serve): $20/mo + PAYG at $10/1M tokens and $1/1M embeddings; 30-day rollover of unused free tokens (small incentive).
- Scale (committed): $1,500/mo for 100M tokens included (equiv $15/1M included) + overage at $6.50/1M. Includes basic SLOs, team seats, dedicated support channel.
- Enterprise: custom committed capacity (reserved GPUs), premium SLOs, longer retention, custom quantization/bring-your-own-model (BYOM) options.

Packaging considerations / tradeoffs:
- Simplicity vs. accuracy: Customers prefer simple per-1K token numbers. But we need to avoid underpricing expensive model usage. Potential solution: present a blended list price + explicit "large-model premium" (e.g., +5x for LLM-large).
- Model routing: default route to cheaper model; customers can opt into higher-cost model per-request (flag). Price differences enforced via API param (model=...).
- Bundles: include embeddings/token bundles to cross-sell; e.g., $0.5/1M tokens + 0.75/1M embeddings if bought together in a pack.
- Free tier abuse: throttle new accounts; require card on file for >X usage to reduce fraud.

Operational levers to reduce cost (and thus allow lower pricing):
- Aggressive batching for async workloads (embeddings, bulk generation).
- Cache entire responses or prefixes per customer.
- Offload small/cheap queries to CPU-hosted quantized runtimes (lower $/hr).
- Autoscale with bin-packing across tenants to maximize GPU utilization.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Get real infra $/hr numbers (A100, H100, lower-cost GPUs) from infra-costs spreadsheet (ask Marco).
- Measure actual tps for our model variants with our runtime (batching profiles). Ticket: PRIC-42.
- Define model premium logic and UI (how to show price differences at API level).
- Decide on committed-token vs reserved-node product for Dedicated. Which converts faster?
- Revisit embedding pricing after measuring end-to-end throughput on embedder model.

Quick action items:
- @Marco: drop perf numbers for 7B/13B/70B on our runtime (p50/p95 throughput, cost/hr) — due EOW.
- @Emily: mock up one-pager pricing table for website with the suggested SKUs.
- Link to infra cost spreadsheet and run a sensitivity table: cost $/hr +/-30%, tps +/-30%, margin target 40/50/60%.

Notes-to-self (brain dump):
- Keep PAYG simple and slightly higher than blended committed price to nudge customers to commit.
- For enterprise, price around reserved-node economics + premium for SLA/support.
- Consider a "model-class" label (cheap/standard/premium) and surface that in usage analytics so customers can optimize spend.

Rough back-of-envelope summary (blended):
- Blended list price for general-purpose hosted generation: ~$8-12 per 1M tokens (depends on mix).
- Blended embedding price: ~$1 per 1M embeddings.
- Committed discounts should range 35-70% depending on commitment size.

End of notes.

(very messy — will refine once infra numbers + perf datapoints available)
